import numpy as np

def apply_move(board, move):
    x, y = move
    # Switch row
    board[x] = 1 - board[x]
    # Switch column
    board[:, y] = 1 - board[:, y]
    # Switch the chosen square back since it was switched twice
    board[x][y] = 1 - board[x][y]

def is_monochrome(board):
    return np.all(board == board[0, 0])

def find_sequence(n=6):
    initial_board = np.array([[((i + j) % 2) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)])
    target_board = np.zeros((n, n))  # Targeting a black board (all 0s)

    # Trying a specific pattern for simplicity: switch each square in the main diagonal
    sequence = [(i, i) for i in range(n)]

    current_board = initial_board.copy()
    for move in sequence:
        apply_move(current_board, move)
    
    if is_monochrome(current_board):
        print(sequence)
    else:
        print("No suitable sequence found.")
